note: Declarative authority for the platform differences between the web build (engine/source/plumline-engine.js, the single editable mathematical source) and the generated Node/add-on mirror (engine/engine.js). The generator engine/generate-engine-mirror.js applies EXACTLY these adaptations and nothing else. No full function bodies are stored here. A third divergence, a widened scope, an adaptation touching another function, or an adaptation changing a mathematical constant must FAIL the checker.

header.mirror_first_line: /* === Plumline engine: the exact same code as the Google Sheets add-on === */
header.reason: The web source opens with the structural ENGINE_START marker (consumed by the Worker engineSource slice). The mirror opens with a plain add-on header comment; it carries no ENGINE_START/ENGINE_END markers because it is a standalone CommonJS/global module, not a Worker slice.

wrapper.reason: Node/add-on consumers require a standalone module that exports a closed API on module.exports and on the global (window/globalThis). The web source is a bare function body composed into the Worker/main-thread interface, so it has no wrapper. The wrapper is platform packaging, not mathematics.

adaptations.reason: On the web every formula's stored value is 0, so folding an unsupported formula to its cached value would inject a false 0; the web build ALWAYS forbids the cached-formula fallback. In the Google Sheets add-on the cached value is exact, so the fallback is safe and allowed by default. The add-on mirror therefore takes an options argument and defaults the fallback to allowed unless a caller explicitly passes false.
adaptations.mirror_behavior: allowCachedFormulaFallback defaults to true (add-on), false only when options.allowCachedFormulaFallback === false
adaptations.provenance: pre-E baseline; the historical hand-maintained mirror already carried this exact divergence

adaptations.reason: The mirror nests the variable-aware formula-limit evaluation inside an explicit `if (variables)` block within `if (limitFormula !== null)`, rather than the web build's combined `if (limitFormula !== null && variables)`. The two are behaviourally identical (the inner block only runs when both are truthy), but the add-on keeps the structure split so the add-on can extend the no-variables branch. No result, error, field or value changes.
adaptations.provenance: pre-E baseline; the historical hand-maintained mirror already carried this exact divergence

forbidden.third_divergence: a third function whose normalized body differs between canonical and generated mirror must fail
forbidden.widened_scope: an adaptation matching zero or multiple sites must fail
forbidden.cross_function: an adaptation editing a function other than its declared target must fail
forbidden.constant_change: an adaptation changing a mathematical constant (ENGINE.*, EPSILON, PIVOT_TOLERANCE, tolerances) must fail

provenance: Derived by AST comparison of engine/source/plumline-engine.js and the historical engine/engine.js: 88 top-level functions in both, 86 with byte-identical or comment-only bodies, exactly 2 functional divergences (newContext_, readConstraint_).
do_not_regenerate: This manifest is the editable authority for platform differences. Editing it changes what the generator is allowed to do. It is NOT regenerated during verify.
